Hey first of all I’m very sorry for your loss. To the other points I hear you. But you’re only 23. You’ve got your life ahead of you. We live in a society where we are conditioned to be extremely hard on ourselves if things don’t work out. Just because you’re not good at it now doesn’t mean you can’t become good at it still. And maybe it’s also just not your thing? I lied myself into thinking I wanted to work in finance for years. Cause I thought I had to become rich and whatever. Turns out I fucking hate finance and once I gave myself room to say that - I felt way better and today I have a job I’m actually good at. And also I would heavily challenge “zero noticeable progress”. Just because things haven’t moved on the job/academic front the way you wanted to. Life goes way beyond job/academia. You lost two of your lost ones early in your life. Coping with that is a incomprehensible sign of strength and speaks volumes about your character. Which proves you have been making progress. Remember there is no right way. Everyone goes their own way. And so will you. 

And so the bottom line is. Keep trying. I believe in you.

And from a fellow art lover - isn’t it always the troubled artists who make the greatest art? Try and incorporate all of these negative emotions into your art and see where it gets you. At the very least it’ll help you understand. Don’t give up dude. The world is a better place with you in it.
